name: Solvang Duster
description:
A knee-length to ankle-length duster in heavy waxed cotton canvas, cut generously through the shoulders and chest with a back split that runs from hem to mid-thigh for ease of movement. Solvang makes this coat in three lengths and four weights; the most popular is the mid-weight in tobacco brown or charcoal, with antique brass press-studs down the front and at the wrist adjusters. The lining is a printed flannel in a small geometric pattern — different every season, always muted. The wax finish gives the coat a slight sheen that develops a patina over years of wear, acquiring creases and darker marks at stress points that become part of the garment's character.

Solvang is a Tier 3 Norwegian-heritage label that has been in the corridor since the 2140s. The duster occupies a comfortable space between working coat and considered fashion — it reads differently depending on who's wearing it and where. On a Tier 3 professional it says deliberate; on a Tier 2 worker it says inherited or saved up for; on a geneware user with a tail or modified lower body it says practical, because the generous cut and back split accommodate anatomy that most coats don't. People who move through multiple zones in a day — fixers, journalists, independent contractors — favor it for exactly that reason.
what_it_says: You move through the world on your own terms and you dress for that movement.
worn_by: anyone who covers ground between zones
story_hooks: A long-term owner's duster has had its wax finish re-applied so many times that the collar is nearly stiff — and pressed into the underside of the collar is the faint impression of a stamp, possibly a corponation seal, that wasn't put there by Solvang
Solvang's flannel lining pattern this season contains a repeated geometric element that a textile analyst claims is a compressed data glyph — the company has not responded to inquiries
Two people show up to the same meeting wearing the same coat in the same color, bought in the same season — one of them is not who they say they are
